hn.sourceOriginalText:
NexusRun — portable AI units

Not a chatbot. An agent that does the work.

Here it is answering a question by going and finding the answer — on a laptop, with no network and no API key. Real output, not a mockup.

nexus run notes-agent -p "When does the launch window open?" running notes-agent:1.0.0 on CPU via llama.cpp/server starting MCP server notes notes v1.0.0 — 2 tool(s): notes__list_notes, notes__read_note → notes__list_notes ({}) ✓ notes__list_notes — launch.txt sites.txt → notes__read_note ({"name":"launch.txt"}) ✓ notes__read_note — The launch window opens on 14 March 2027. The launch window opens on 14 March 2027. — 54 tokens · 7.0 tok/s · 2 tool call(s) over 3 turns # nexus.yaml — the whole agent apiVersion: nexusrun.dev/v1 name: notes-agent version: 1.0.0 models: # already pulled with Ollama? reuse it - source: ollama:llama3.1:8b entrypoint: type: chat system_prompt: | Answer using the n.

Its tools come with it

Tool servers are dependencies, pinned like any other. Nobody has to install anything first, and each one is confined by the kernel to the paths you listed — undeclared means denied.

Secrets stay out of the artifact

The file says which key it needs. The value lives encrypted on the machine that runs it, so the agent is safe to commit and safe to share.

It's built for machines you don't control.

Someone else's laptop, a rack of mixed hardware, a kiosk in a shop, a box that has never seen the internet. That is where agents actually have to work, and where the usual assumptions quietly fail.

It runs where your data already is

On the machine that holds the records, behind the VLAN, or on a box with no network at all. Seal the model in and carry one file across. Nothing is uploaded, and running it more often costs nothing extra.

Verified: imported to an empty machine and generated with no network at all.

It won't quietly use the wrong one

A good GPU the installed runtime was never built to drive is the normal case, and most tools fall back to the CPU without a word. This one says so — then scores the agent on that machine, because answers change with the hardware and the model, not just the prompt.

Verified: a model that scored 0/3 there was rejected and a better one chosen, automatically, per machine.

Safe to run someone else's agent

Read the file, see exactly what it will reach for, then run it knowing the kernel holds it to that. Its tools, its files, its network — nothing it did not declare is possible.

Verified from inside the sandbox: no stray file writes, no outbound connections.

NexusRun doesn't replace llama.cpp or Ollama — it runs on top of them. What it adds is the packaging, the sharing, and the straight answers.

Writes one small YAML file. Edit the prompt to make it yours.

Straight from the folder, so you can change the prompt and go again.

A few hundred bytes, to any registry you already use. No network at the other end? nexus build --seal packs the model in so it travels on a USB stick.

The runtime is free forever. NexusRun Cloud hosts and signs your units for teams shipping to real fleets — early access is open .

hn.sourceTextZh:
NexusRun — 便攜式人工智慧單元不是聊天機器人。做這項工作的代理人。在這裡，它透過在筆記型電腦上尋找答案來回答問題，沒有網絡，也沒有 API 金鑰。真實輸出，而不是模型。何時打開？ →notes__read_note({"name":"launch.txt"}) ✓notes__read_note — 啟動視窗於 3 月 14 日開啟2027 年。啟動窗口於 2027 年 3 月 14 日開放。 — 54 個代幣 · 7.0 tok/s · 2 個工具調用超過 3 輪 # nexus.yaml — 整個代理 apiVersion: nexusrun.dev/v1 name: Notes-agent version: 1.0.0 models: # 已經與 Ollama 一起拉取了嗎？重複使用它 - 來源：ollama:llama3.1:8b 入口點：類型：聊天系統提示： |使用 n 回答。它附帶的工具工具伺服器是依賴項，像其他任何工具一樣固定。沒有人必須先安裝任何東西，並且每個都被核心限制在您列出的路徑中 - 未聲明意味著被拒絕。秘密遠離工件 該文件說明了它需要哪個密鑰。該值在運行它的電腦上以加密方式存在，因此代理可以安全地提交和共用。它是為您無法控制的機器而建造的。

別人的筆記型電腦、混合硬體的機架、商店中的資訊亭、從未見過網路的盒子。這就是代理人實際上必須工作的地方，也是通常的假設悄悄失效的地方。它在您的資料所在的位置運作 在保存記錄的電腦上、VLAN 後面或根本沒有網路的盒子上。將模型密封起來並攜帶一份文件穿過。沒有上傳任何內容，並且更頻繁地運行它不需要任何額外費用。已驗證：導入到空機器並在完全沒有網路的情況下產生。它不會悄悄地使用錯誤的一個好的 GPU，但安裝的運行時從未構建用於驅動，這是正常情況，並且大多數工具會不言而喻地回退到 CPU。這個人是這樣說的——然後對那台機器上的代理進行評分，因為答案會隨著硬體和模型的變化而變化，而不僅僅是提示的變化。已驗證：得分 0/3 的模型被拒絕，每台機器自動選擇更好的模型。安全地運行其他人的代理讀取該文件，準確查看它將達到什麼目的，然後運行它，知道核心會保留它。它的工具、它的檔案、它的網路——它沒有聲明的一切都是可能的。從沙箱內部驗證：沒有雜散文件寫入，沒有出站連線。 NexusRun 不會取代 llama.cpp 或 Ollama — 它在它們之上運行。它增加的是包裝、分享和直接答案。寫入一個小 YAML 檔案。

編輯提示以使其成為您的提示。直接從資料夾中，這樣您就可以更改提示並再次進行。幾百個字節，到您已經使用的任何註冊表。另一端沒有網路？ nexus build --seal 將模型打包在 USB 記憶棒上。運行時是永久免費的。 NexusRun Cloud 託管並簽署您的設備，以便團隊運送到真實車隊 - 早期訪問已開放。

hn.originalTitle: Show HN: Notula – where humans edit the Markdown your AI agents read
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Notula - WYSIWYG Markdown editor for docs as code

WYSIWYG Markdown editor. For the docs in your git repo.

Docs as code , without having to be a coder. Like Google Docs , on files that never leave the repository : comment on a passage, reply, resolve, browse the docs in a tree, and publish without anybody being shown a rebase .

Free, and it stays free. No account, no server. macOS and Windows.

Your documentation already moved.

Your tools did not. What docs as code costs a team .

AI writes Markdown

Agents read, write and review plain .md natively. Files in the repo are where they are strongest, and where your engineers already review changes.

So the docs followed

Specs, PRDs, RFCs and runbooks left the wiki and landed next to the code. That was the right call, and nobody is moving them back.

And everyone else lost their tools

No comments, no threads, no way to browse, no way to edit a paragraph without learning a code editor, a diff and a rebase first.

Everything you use in Google Docs,

on files that never leave your repository.

Speaks git and nothing else, so it works with what you have

Only the documentation, none of the code

Open a repository with thousands of source files and get a clean tree of Markdown. Folders with no documents in them never appear.

WYSIWYG, not live preview

No Markdown syntax, ever. No hashes, no asterisks, no table pipes, not even on the line your cursor is on. The file on disk stays ordinary Markdown.

Mermaid diagrams draw themselves

A mermaid block is a picture in the document, not a wall of arrows and brackets. On disk it is still the same fenced block, so it draws on the host too.

The comments you actually miss

Select a passage, leave a comment, reply, resolve.

Git, without teaching git

Every version of the document is there to read and to bring back. Nobody is ever shown a rebase, a stash, or the words detached HEAD.

You are never the last to know

and nothing ever changes under your cursor.

Somebody named you

Your machine tells you, with the sentence they wrote.

Maya Chen named you

Is the order the real problem, or the number of fields?

checkout-redesign.md · platform-docs

Clicking it opens the document at that paragraph, not at the top.

It keeps watching repositories you do not have open, with the window closed.

Two at a time arrive on their own; more than that arrive together, so they stay read.

And you did not have to go and ask.

Every document the rest of the team has moved on is marked in the tree, with who moved it and when.

Your own unpublished work is marked the same way, so nothing waits in a drawer you forgot about.

It looks every thirty seconds while you are working, and every few minutes while you are not.

All of it is read from the fetched branch, so the document on screen is still exactly what you left until you take the change.

Threads that live in the repository

A conversation is committed next to the document it is about, so it arrives with the clone and outlives every account.

Documents stay clean. No invisible anchors, no block IDs, no HTML comments.

Anchored by the quoted passage and its context, following the W3C Web Annotation model.

An append-only log with a union merge driver, so two people commenting at once cannot conflict.

Navigates like a browser

Follow a link and the document opens in the same pane. Back and forward return you to exactly where you were, scroll position included.

Every pane keeps its own trail, so a reference held open in a split is never disturbed.

Relative links between documents resolve the way they do on the host.

Non-Markdown link targets open read-only instead of being handed to another app.

A one-character edit stays a one-character diff

Notula writes back only what changed. Across 6,000 real documents, 96.4% of blocks survive an edit untouched.

Your agent gets a briefing, not a guess

Notula writes down how the workspace works, and points Claude Code at it.

It writes notula-agents.md describing the document types, the fields, the layout and the commands, and borrows three lines of your CLAUDE.md to point at it. It never overwrites what you wrote there.

The briefing carries the rules that are invisible once broken. Renaming a document is notula docs move , because the comment log is filed under the document's path and a plain mv orphans every thread on it.

There is a command line behind that - documents, types, fields, status, all with --json - so an agent operates the workspace instead of guessing at files.

Notula - 用於文件的所見即所得 Markdown 編輯器作為程式碼所見即所得 Markdown 編輯器.對於 git 儲存庫中的文件。文件即代碼，無需成為編碼員。與 Google Docs 一樣，對於永遠不會離開儲存庫的文件：對段落進行評論、回應、解析、瀏覽樹中的文件以及在沒有任何人顯示變基的情況下進行發布。免費，而且一直免費。沒有帳戶，沒有伺服器。 macOS 和 Windows。您的文件已經移動。你的工具沒有。文件作為程式碼需要團隊付出代價。 AI 編寫 Markdown 代理程式以本機方式讀取、寫入和審查純 .md。儲存庫中的文件是最強大的，並且您的工程師已經在其中審查了更改。因此，遵循規範、PRD、RFC 和操作手冊的文件離開了 wiki，落在了程式碼旁邊。這是正確的決定，沒有人會把它們撤回來。其他人都失去了他們的工具沒有評論，沒有線程，沒有辦法瀏覽，沒有辦法在不先學習程式碼編輯器、差異和變基的情況下編輯段落。您在 Google 文件中使用的所有內容，以及從未離開儲存庫的文件。只講 git，不講任何其他內容，因此它可以與您擁有的內容一起工作。 只有文檔，沒有任何程式碼。 開啟一個包含數千個原始檔案的儲存庫，並取得一個乾淨的 Markdown 樹。其中沒有文件的資料夾永遠不會出現。所見即所得，不是即時預覽 永遠沒有 Markdown 語法。

hn.originalTitle: Launch HN: Bullet (YC S26) – A Faster Coding Agent
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Bullet · Fast, by design.

A REALLY FAST CODING AGENT

Bullet routes, searches, and executes with one purpose: keeping up with you.

LEANER BY DEFAULT.

Same model → tools → results pattern. A tighter loop around it.

Right model. Right moment.

Route straightforward work to fast models. Escalate only when the mission demands it.

Acquire the target. Ignore the noise.

Targeted search and file reads find relevant code without embedding the whole repo.

Never queue what can run together.

Independent tool calls execute in parallel. Duplicate calls and stuck loops are intercepted before they waste another second.

SEE BULLET IN ACTION.

Real prompt. Real repository. No cinematic shortcuts.

NO GUI. SAME AGENT.

Same router, tools, and agent loop. Now it lives in your shell.

$ npm install -g @trybullet/cli

macOS & Linux · Node 18+ · free, no key required to start

BUILT OUT OF FRUSTRATION.

At our company, we were burning hours waiting on agent runs. We were building with Claude Code every day, watching capable models move through needlessly slow machinery.

So Bullet began as a passion project: route simple work faster, read only what matters, run independent tools together, and stop loops before they spiral.

We use it internally now. It saved us a headache. We thought it might save you one too.

DON'T LET YOUR CODE HOLD YOU HOSTAGE.

Free to use. No subscriptions. Just a faster way to ship.

1667 · write your novel in the terminal

Write your novel in the terminal.

1667 asks a model for the next paragraph, then keeps every take it gives you side by side on a tree you can walk back through. Your keys, your endpoint, your files on your disk. No analytics, no telemetry, no account anywhere in the source.

Installs 1667 0.9.9. Supports macOS arm64/x64 and glibc 2.17+ Linux arm64/x64. Run 1667 upgrade for later managed releases.

Installs 1667 0.9.9 on Windows x64. Exit 1667 and run this command again to install a later release.

Needs Node 22. npm manages this installation. Use npm to install later releases.

Needs Bun 1.3.14 or later, and Node 22. Git manages this installation.

This optional path needs GitHub CLI. It verifies version 0.9.9 before it runs the local file.

macOS · Linux · Windows

⟷ drag or use arrow keys to pan

Fullscreen unavailable. Open the demo video →

1667 homepage demo The opening write view shows “The lantern keeper,” chapter three, parts 11 through 13. Part 12 is on take 3 of 5: “He did not move toward the stairs. Instead he set the brass compass on the bar between them, and its needle went around twice, slow, like a dog deciding whether to lie down, and stopped pointing at Maren. ‘Has the cliff road ever been walked at night without a light?’ he asked. ‘Not by anyone who came back,’ she said. The needle shivered and held.” Compose: Enter opens the composer. The direction “let the unlit lantern answer” is typed and submitted. The generated next part reads: “The lantern flame bent toward the compass, though no door had opened.” The pro.

Up and down select a story part; left and right select one of its sibling takes without deleting the others.

The path map shows one row per part, sibling takes as circles, and word counts at right; the arrow keys move its cursor.

Press ? to open the complete keyboard reference, then use Page Down to read the remaining commands.

$ scroll to continue

It drafts. You decide what stays.

You move through a manuscript, and the model writes a paragraph when you ask it to. Then it stops and waits for you.

◉ ◎ ◎ Ask again, keep both Ask for another version of a paragraph and the one you were reading stays where it is. The new take sits beside it, and ← and → flip between them. Every take you generate stays on the tree, and d is the only thing that removes one.

├─┬─╴ The shape is a tree A story is a tree of parts and takes. The story line is the path you have selected through it. Branches you walked away from are still there, and still yours to come back to.

~/book It lives in a folder Stories sit in a directory you chose. Export writes Markdown next to them. There is no server to sign in to and nothing to migrate off later.

Every draft you didn't keep, still there.

Ask for another take and the one you were reading does not go anywhere. It becomes a sibling. Press m and the shape of the whole thing opens up: the line you are on, the forks you made, and the paragraphs you wrote once and walked away from.

Three views, cycled with the same key. Nothing is archived, nothing is pruned on your behalf, and d is the only thing that removes a take.

hn.originalTitle: What We Learned Moving Our Agent Loops from Anthropic to GLM
hn.sourceOriginalText:
What We Learned Moving Our Agent Loops to GLM

What We Learned Moving Our Agent Loops from Anthropic to GLM

Why we moved most of Unblocked's agent traffic from Claude Opus to GLM 5.2, what the blind A/Bs and the ledger actually showed, and what broke on the way.

TL;DR: We moved most of Unblocked's agent traffic from Claude Opus to GLM 5.2.

“Per-token” math promised 95% savings; per-task production reality delivered 68%. Getting there took blind A/B evaluation on real code reviews, a circuit-broken multi-provider serving pool, and weeks of "OpenAI-compatible" surprises.

Background: Unblocked gives agents the organizational understanding of your best engineers. Its context engine connects and reconciles knowledge across your code, conversations, issues, documentation, and production systems, then makes that understanding available wherever work happens. Agents access context through MCP/CLI/APIs and Unblocked products like Code Review and Unblocked Code apply that context directly to reviewing and writing code. The result is better software, produced with fewer tokens, fewer iterations, and less back-and-forth.

For most of the last two years, Unblocked ran on Anthropic models. Our product is a set of agentic loops: answering engineering questions, reviewing code, searching across an organization's institutional knowledge. Claude Opus sat in the outer loop of nearly all of it.

This summer we moved most of that traffic to GLM, an open-weight model served by third-party inference providers. This post covers why we did it, what we measured, what broke, and where we've landed. We're not going to describe our system internals, but the findings should transfer to anyone running agent loops at scale.

When we audited our AI spend, one number stood out: over 80% of it came from frontier model usage in our main agent loops, almost entirely Opus.

We listed the knobs available to us:

Model. The single biggest factor in output quality for code review, less so for Q&A.

Turns. Less important than expected once caching is optimized for long loops.

Tools. Variable, and growing as features ship.

Caching. Already optimized. Aggressive prompt caching holds us above a 95% cache hit rate turn-over-turn, so there was nothing meaningful left to reclaim there.

Prompts. Mostly optimized, and mattering less with every model generation.

Caching and prompts were tapped out. Deleting features wasn't on the table. That left the model itself, and the gap between frontier pricing and open-weight pricing had become impossible to ignore. GLM 5.2 was billed at less than a third of frontier rates, and on raw per-token pricing across serving providers the savings looked closer to 95% against Opus.

The question was whether the quality held up in production, on real workloads, judged by real users. Benchmarks weren't going to answer that.

Per-token pricing is a lie you tell yourself #

The first correction came fast. One of our engineers pulled real usage off the Fireworks dashboard: 2.35 billion tokens served for roughly 5% of what the same volume would have cost on Opus, with caching accounted for on both sides. A 95% cost reduction, on paper.

Then we ran the same code review on the same commit, same PR, same prompt, once with Opus and once with GLM. The real-world saving was 68%, not 95%.

The arithmetic is multiplicative, and only one of the two terms is printed on the rate card:

text effective cost = token price × tokens required per task On price alone, GLM looked like a 20× improvement. On the bill it was about 3.1×.

The gap is behavioral. GLM uses far more tokens per task than Opus does:

It makes more tool calls. It explores more aggressively, which is sometimes good and sometimes waste.

It makes more mistakes, and mistakes cost turns. A malformed search or an empty result means another round trip through the loop.

It ingests larger tool results and spends more tokens reasoning about them.

It's more talkative in general.

This isn't an anecdote from a handful of samples. In our search flow, average tokens per call rose from about 18,500 to about 24,700 (up a third) over the migration window, and GLM was only serving around 45% of those calls. The exploration overhead is visible in the fleet-wide ledger.

So the metric that matters is cost per task, not cost per token. Any team evaluating a model swap should run identical workloads end to end and compare invoices, not rate cards. A 68% reduction is still an enormous win. It's just not the win the rate card promised.

我們學到了什麼 將我們的代理循環轉移到 GLM 我們學到了什麼 將我們的代理循環從 Anthropic 轉移到 GLM 為什麼我們將 Unblocked 的大部分代理流量從 Claude Opus 轉移到 GLM 5.2，盲 A/B 和賬本實際顯示的內容，以及途中發生的情況。 TL;DR：我們將 Unblocked 的大部分代理流量從 Claude Opus 移至 GLM 5.2。 「每個代幣」數學承諾節省 95%；每項任務的生產實際交付率為 68%。實現這一目標需要對真實程式碼審查進行盲目 A/B 評估、斷路的多提供者服務池以及數週的「OpenAI 相容」驚喜。背景：Unblocked 使代理商能夠在組織上了解您最好的工程師。它的上下文引擎可以連接並協調程式碼、對話、問題、文件和生產系統中的知識，然後使這種理解在工作發生的任何地方都可用。代理透過 MCP/CLI/API 存取上下文，並且 Unblocked 產品（例如 Code Review 和 Unblocked Code）將該上下文直接應用於審查和編寫程式碼。結果是更好的軟體，用更少的代幣、更少的迭代和更少的來回生產。在過去兩年的大部分時間裡，Unblocked 都在人類模型上運行。我們的產品是一組代理循環：回答工程問題、審查代碼、搜尋組織的機構知識。克勞德·奧普斯 (Claude Opus) 幾乎位於所有區域的外環。

今年夏天，我們將大部分流量轉移到了 GLM，這是一個由第三方推理提供者提供服務的開放權重模型。這篇文章介紹了我們這樣做的原因、我們測量了什麼、出現了什麼問題以及我們的成果。我們不會描述我們的系統內部結構，但研究結果應該轉移給大規模運行代理循環的任何人。當我們審計我們的人工智慧支出時，有一個數字很引人注目：其中 80% 以上來自我們主要代理循環中的前沿模型使用，幾乎全部是 Opus。我們列出了可用的旋鈕：型號。程式碼審查輸出品質的最大因素，而問答的影響較小。輪流。一旦針對長循環優化了緩存，就沒有預期那麼重要了。工具。可變的，並且隨著功能的發布而不斷增長。快取.已經優化了。積極的提示快取使我們的快取命中率高於 95%，因此沒有任何有意義的東西可以回收。提示。大多數情況下都進行了最佳化，並且對於每一代模型來說影響較小。快取和提示已被淘汰。刪除功能不在桌面上。這就只剩下模型本身了，前沿定價和開放權重定價之間的差距已經變得無法忽視。 GLM 5.2 的計費價格不到前沿費率的三分之一，根據服務提供者的原始每個代幣定價，與 Opus 相比，節省了接近 95%。

問題在於，在生產中、在實際工作負載上、由真實使用者判斷時，品質是否穩定。基準不會回答這個問題。每個代幣的定價是你告訴自己的一個謊言 # 第一次修正來得很快。我們的一位工程師從 Fireworks 儀表板中獲得了實際使用：23.5 億個代幣的費用大約是 Opus 上相同數量代幣成本的 5%，雙方都考慮了快取。理論上成本降低了 95%。然後我們在相同的提交、相同的 PR、相同的提示下執行相同的程式碼審查，一次使用 Opus，一次使用 GLM。現實世界的節省率為 68%，而不是 95%。算術是乘法，並且只在價目表上列印這兩個術語中的一個：文字有效成本 = 代幣價格 × 每個任務所需的代幣 僅就價格而言，GLM 看起來像是 20 倍的改進。帳單上大約是 3.1 倍。差距是行為上的。 GLM 在每個任務中使用的令牌比 Opus 多得多：它呼叫了更多的工具。它更積極地探索，這有時是好的，有時是浪費。它會犯更多的錯誤，而錯誤會導致輪換。格式錯誤的搜尋或空白結果意味著循環的另一次往返。它吸收更大的工具結果並花費更多的代幣來推理它們。整體來說還是比較健談的。這並不是來自少數樣本的軼事。

在我們的搜尋流程中，在遷移視窗中，每次調用的平均代幣從約 18,500 個上升到約 24,700 個（上升了三分之一），而 GLM 僅服務了其中約 45% 的呼叫。探索開銷在整個艦隊的分類帳中可見。因此，重要的指標是每個任務的成本，而不是每個代幣的成本。任何評估模型交換的團隊都應該端到端運行相同的工作負載並比較發票，而不是價目表。 68% 的減少仍然是一個巨大的勝利。這並不是價目表所承諾的勝利。我們如何

hn.originalTitle: Do All Your Agents Need Models Like Claude 5 or GPT-5.6?
hn.titleZh: 您的所有代理商都需要 Claude 5 或 GPT-5.6 等型號嗎？
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Claude / OpenAI / Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
您所有的代理商真的需要 Claude 5 或 GPT-5.6 這樣的型號嗎？ | AIMOWAY 部落格 人工智慧代理系統正變得越來越普遍。它們可以顯著提高生產力，但一旦代理工作流程開始在計劃者、工作人員、審閱者、工具和重試之間進行重複調用，模型成本的增長速度可能會比預期快得多。 Claude Fable 5 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 等旗艦型號專為艱鉅的工作而打造。它們提供前沿程度的推理、指令遵循、工具使用和長期代理能力，代表了大語言模型工程的前沿。這種能力的建設成本和服務成本都很高。大規模訓練和運行這些模型需要大規模的運算集群、先進的加速器、高效能網路、冷卻基礎設施和大量的電力。其中一些成本不可避免地會出現在推理定價中，對於任何大規模營運代理商的人來說，也會出現在每月的帳單中。因此，值得問一個相當簡單的問題：您的所有代理人實際上都需要這種程度的情報嗎？人們使用人工智慧代理做什麼？在現實世界的工作流程中，人工智慧代理執行廣泛的任務。有些確實需要高級推理。許多人沒有。典型的座席工作負載包括：閱讀、分類、總結和路由電子郵件、文件、票證和訊息；

從非結構化文字中提取結構化資訊；搜尋文件、原始程式碼、資料庫、日誌和知識庫；生成報告、摘要、會議記錄和日常商務信函；翻譯、重寫或重組現有內容；格式化資料並在模式或文件格式之間轉換資訊；編寫、審查、測試和記錄代碼；監控系統、日誌、佇列、儀表板和計劃作業；系統、問題追蹤器和專案管理系統；根據預先定義的標準比較產品、記錄、配置或文件；進行日常研究並從多個來源收集資訊；將較大的工作流程分解為較小的任務並將其分派給專門的子代理；檢查操作是否滿足預定義的規則、策略或約束；產生初記初記、手動審核、手動審核；在一些明顯的情況下，使用最強大的可用模型是有意義的：重大架構決策、微妙的安全審查、模糊的法律文件、複雜的科學問題或重要的商業決策。

這些任務是困難的、重要的，或者兩者兼而有之。但它們並不代表代理系統內的每個模型呼叫。在大型工作流程中，它們可能只佔總活動的一小部分。前沿模型越來越針對編碼進行最佳化，但代理商所做的不僅僅是程式碼軟體工程已成為前沿模型開發中最明顯的戰場之一。現在，領先的供應商在展示和評估其最強大的模型時，非常重視編碼、代理編碼、長期運行的軟體工程任務、終端使用、工具執行和自主開發工作流程。當前的前沿版本反映了這一重點。 OpenAI 強調了 GPT-5.6 Sol 在編碼和涉及規劃、迭代和工具協調的長期工程工作流程方面的性能，而 Anthropic 將 Claude Fable 5 定位為最適合雄心勃勃的編碼項目和長期運行的代理工作的模型。這是有充分理由的。軟體開發是產生人工智慧最明顯的具有商業意義的應用之一。程式碼是高度結構化的，工程工作具有經濟價值，通常可以使用編譯器、測試套件、靜態分析、CI 系統和其他確定性工具自動檢查輸出。專用編碼劑本身也已成為重要的產品。

因此，激勵措施異常強烈：軟體工程對於人工智慧代理來說既是一個技術上有吸引力的環境，也是一個可以將更好的模型性能轉化為明顯經濟價值的市場。然而，代理工作的很大一部分與編寫軟體無關。上面列出的工作負載中只有一部分本質上與生成或修改程式碼有關：編寫、審查、測試、記錄和分析
